title: Furbo
summary: An AI sports buddy you text on WhatsApp: predictions, live news and banter about your team.
body:
## The idea

Following your team means jumping between apps, group chats and score sites. Furbo puts all of that in the one place fans already live: a WhatsApp chat. You text it like a friend and it answers with predictions, the latest news and opinions about your team.

## What I built

- A conversational agent built with LangChain on Azure OpenAI that keeps up with sports news and talks about it in a natural, fan-like way.
- The WhatsApp channel through Twilio, plus a web version with English and Spanish.
- Accounts, subscriptions with Stripe and transactional emails.

## Where it's going

The web and WhatsApp MVP works, and I'm pausing it to explore a bigger idea: putting the same AI brain inside licensed team plush toys, so the conversation happens with something you can actually hold.

title: ElAtletico
summary: A Spanish-language digital sports paper and daily newsletter, researched and written by an AI pipeline.
body:
## The idea

Mexican sports fans read most of their news in English or in clickbait. El Atlético is a clean, multi-sport paper in Spanish, with a daily newsletter, that covers Liga MX, the big European leagues, NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL and UFC.

## What I built

- **A content pipeline in Python** that runs on a cron job on a Raspberry Pi. It pulls news from ESPN's public API, filters and de-duplicates stories, picks a balanced set every day across sports and teams, and writes each article with OpenAI models.
- **A deterministic verifier that acts as the editor.** Clean articles publish themselves; anything suspicious stays hidden with the reason logged, so a bad note never reaches readers.
- **The site and newsletter** in Next.js, reading only what the verifier approved.

## What I learned

The first version ran on n8n. Rebuilding it as plain Python jobs made it cheaper (around a third of a cent per article), easier to test and much easier to reason about when something goes wrong.

title: Hablar con Santa
summary: Parents buy a call and Santa phones their kid, with an AI voice that asks about their wish list.
body:
## The idea

A seasonal product for Mexican parents: buy a pack of calls, type your kid's name and phone number, and Santa calls them in Spanish.

## What I built

- **The voice call flow**: Santa's personality is a long, carefully tuned prompt that spends most of the call on the kid's wish list, asks follow-up questions about each gift and never breaks character.
- **Credits that can't be lost**: a credit is taken before the call is placed and refunded automatically if the call fails.
- **A gift summary for parents**: after each call, a structured summary of what the kid asked for is emailed to the parent.
- Stripe checkout without forcing an account, so buying a call takes a minute.

## What's next

For the next season I'm moving off the current voice provider and working on a video call with an animated Santa character.
